questions.q: What is the defining feature of a star schema?
options: One central fact table, connected directly to several dimension tables, each exactly one join away
Every table in the database joins to every other table
There is no fact table at all, only dimensions
All tables must be physically stored on the same disk
questions.explain: The 'one hop' rule — every dimension joins directly to the fact table, never dimension-to-dimension — is what makes it look like a star.

questions.q: Why are dimension tables in a star schema often denormalized?
options: Fewer joins means faster aggregate queries, and dimension tables are small enough that the duplication cost barely matters
SQL Server requires all dimension tables to be denormalized
Denormalization is accidental and considered a design flaw
It's impossible to normalize a dimension table under any circumstances
questions.explain: This is a deliberate tradeoff, breaking Chapter 11's 3NF rule on purpose for query speed.

questions.q: In the real AdventureWorksDW2014 example, how many joins does it take to get from FactInternetSales to DimCustomer?
options: One direct join
Two joins, through DimProduct first
Three joins, through DimDate and DimSalesTerritory
It's impossible to join FactInternetSales to DimCustomer at all
questions.explain: Every dimension in a star schema sits exactly one join away from the fact table — that's the whole point.

questions.q: Why do BI tools and reporting engines often expect a star schema by default?
options: Because every dimension is exactly one join away, the query optimizer has an easy, well-understood shape to work with
Star schemas are the only shape SQL Server supports
BI tools cannot read normalized tables at all
Star schemas eliminate the need for any dimension tables
questions.explain: The predictable, simple join pattern makes star schemas fast and easy for query optimizers and BI tools alike.

questions.q: How does a star-schema dimension table's design differ from a fully-normalized OLTP table from Chapter 11?
options: It often flattens related attributes (like category and subcategory names) directly onto one row, instead of splitting them into separate normalized tables
It has no primary key, unlike any OLTP table
It cannot contain any foreign keys
It must have exactly the same structure as its OLTP source table
questions.explain: This flattening is the deliberate denormalization that distinguishes a warehouse dimension from a Chapter 11-style normalized table.
